title: Using Bibliometric Analysis and Machine Learning to Identify Compounds Binding to Sialidase-1.
summary: A Bayesian model ranked three candidates for testing; microscale thermophoresis found sialidase-1 binding for sulfameter (Kd 2.15 ± 1.02 μM) and mexenone (8.88 ± 4.02 μM). Enzyme activity and chaperone function were not tested.

evidence.tested: Three selected compounds were tested by microscale thermophoresis in triplicate against 5 nM recombinant human sialidase-1; two bound, with reported Kd values of 2.15 ± 1.02 μM (sulfameter) and 8.88 ± 4.02 μM (mexenone).
evidence.unknown: The paper states that the target model used a small training set and limited chemical space. The study measured binding, not sialidase activity, cellular chaperoning, or disease benefit.
evidence.ai_role: Assay Central used ECFP6 descriptors and a Bayesian model trained on curated ChEMBL and BindingDB IC50 data to rank compounds; toxicity and CNS filters also informed candidate selection.

source_review.scope: Full PMC paper, including Methods, results and limitations.
